parsed.explanation: Thin-data jurisdiction. No trans-specific criminal statute, no documented targeting, and no documented traveler-facing exposure (no facility bans, no police sweeps, no trans violence record). One protective rule operates in immigration detention (2014 non-discrimination on gender identity). But no recognition machinery, no general protections, opaque prison placement, same-sex unions illegal, and a near-bottom equality index — a real climate caution. Extrapolation: a state that repealed its sodomy code and signed the 2011 SOGI statement shows no hostile enforcement architecture; absence of documented harm in thin data is not safety, so it sits just above the reduced band, not higher.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented; marker-recognition practice at entry is an open question.
entry_documents.interaction: Whether foreign documents with markers are accepted is unknown; no documented refusals or secondary screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Criminal-justice prison placement for trans prisoners wholly undocumented; potential birth-sex placement is an unquantified exposure.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: 2014 immigration-detention rules bar gender-identity discrimination in the processing centre.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Protection limited to immigration detention; does not reach the corrections system, and enforcement is unsourced.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility-access rules documented; bathrooms, wards, spa settings unevidenced.

care_services.exposure: No documented denial of care; HRT import and refill access unevidenced.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No trans-specific police enforcement documented; no morality police or sweeps in the record.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State diplomatically supported SOGI rights (2011 statement signatory).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: No employment-discrimination protection and no recognition could leave an outed traveller without recourse if hostility occurs, but no documented incidents.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated trans-violence incidents or rate documented; social climate unknown, index placement near bottom suggests possible everyday disapproval.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response to anti-trans violence is unsourced; recourse would be informal at best.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No general anti-discrimination recourse; same-sex unions illegal; enforcement of the one detention rule unverified.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Immigration-detention non-discrimination rule exists as paper remedy.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: If outed in an adverse encounter, documented remedies are thin.

anchor_checks.comparison: Higher than this anchor: 0.45-B documents active facility exclusion and care denial with enforcement; this dossier documents no such exposures, only gaps.
Similar to slightly above: 0.55-B documents border secondary screening friction; here even that is undocumentated, but thin data and bottom-tier equality index keep it near the same tier.
Below this anchor: 0.75-C documents working remedies, trained officers and counsel access; this jurisdiction has no documented operating protections beyond one detention rule.
Clearly above: 0.35-A documents a universal exclusion register with routine enforcement; no such state-facing mechanism is documented here at all.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime shows decriminalisation (2016), diplomatic SOGI support, and a single functioning-scope protection inside immigration detention — no documented traveler-facing restriction, targeting, or violence. Against the precedence ladder, the worst documented feature is tier 5 at most (absence of protections, not active exposure), with two open questions: prison placement and everyday social climate (near-bottom equality index, no anti-discrimination law, unions illegal). Per thin-data extrapolation, structural signals — repeal, no morality enforcement, one protective instrument — point away from high risk, but silence is not safety and recourse is minimal if hostility materialises. This places the jurisdiction at the floor of Reduced Risk.
